brief.headline: The exchange reopened and answered the question this desk had left open for five straight sessions: prompt aluminium finally paid up. Cash settled $3,327.50, a fresh cycle high, the curve flipped out of contango into a $7.00 backwardation, four of five base metals rose together - and it all happened on the day Tehran publicly said the strait will NOT reopen while the US naval posture continues, repudiating the very assumption that had knocked the front end down on 05-August.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: LME cash aluminium settled $3,327.50 on 10-August, up $48.00 (+1.46%), the biggest daily gain of the month, a fourth new cycle high in seven sessions and the highest official cash since 22-June. The 3-month settled $3,320.50, up $40.50. Exchange stock fell another 1,500 t to 254,900 t - a 29th consecutive draw and the lowest this century. The whole board rolled onto one genuinely new session, with the English overview, German overview and cache-busted per-metal table all agreeing exactly.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE PREVIOUS THREE HIGHS: this one came with confirmation rather than against it. Cash rose MORE than the 3-month, flipping the curve from a $0.50 contango into a $7.00 backwardation - the first real prompt premium since 04-August and the end of a four-session failure to rebuild. And the complex came along: aluminium +1.23%, lead +0.63%, copper +0.43%, nickel +0.18% on the 3-month, with only zinc lower. On 07-August aluminium had made its high essentially alone while copper gave back $215.

WHY IT HAPPENED: Iran's Foreign Ministry said publicly on 10-August that the strait will not reopen while the US naval posture continues, that Washington has no standing to demand it, and that Iran and Oman have STILL not finalised the safe-navigation statement. The 05-August routing announcement had been priced as the corridor normalising; the issuing government has now said it is not. Brent rose 4.19% in 24 hours to $87.85 on the same news, which matters twice over - as a risk signal and as a cost input, since energy is 30-40% of smelter cash cost.

WHAT TO WATCH, AND THE HONEST CAVEATS: the $7.00 backwardation is thin - about 0.21% of cash, one session old, and almost exactly the July average of $6.48, so this is a repair to normal rather than a squeeze. Three things cut against the bull case: the LME draw rate is decelerating (1,500-1,750 t/day versus 2,000-2,400 t/day in late July) and China's destocking pace is narrowing too; supply outside China is returning, with daily average output up 1.6% month-on-month on Middle East and Iceland restarts; and the 30-year US Treasury yield hit a 19-year high of 5.27%, which tightens liquidity for exactly this kind of positioning-sensitive trade. Today's 13:20 London ring is the clean test of whether the backwardation holds a second day.

Over the five sessions of August cash has added $131.50 (+4.11%) from the 31-July official of $3,196.00, and $166.00 (+5.25%) from the 28-July swing low of $3,159.50. WHAT MAKES THIS PRINT DIFFERENT FROM THE LAST FOUR HIGHS: it was made WITH the complex rather than against it, and it was made WITH the curve rather than against it. Westmetall LME officials, 10-Aug-2026 session. THE RING REOPENED ON MONDAY AND THE ENTIRE BOARD ROLLED TOGETHER ONTO ONE UNIFORM NEW SESSION - there is no carried figure anywhere on this page for the first time in three runs. This compile runs at roughly 04:55 London on Tuesday 11-August, ahead of today's 13:20 ring, so the 10-August official is the latest PUBLISHED official and today's prints after this report. kpis.note: 10-Aug 3-MONTH OFFICIAL $3,320.50 against $3,280.00 = +$40.50 (+1.23%). The 3M rose LESS than cash (+$48.00), which is the arithmetic that produced the structure flip described in the spread row - the front end outbid the forward curve for the first time in six sessions. SECONDARY, DIFFERENT-BASIS REFERENCES FOR THE SAME DAY, QUOTED ONLY AS CORROBORATION AND NOT MIXED INTO THIS ROW: SMM's 11-August aluminium morning briefing reports the LME evening close at $3,346.50 (+0.34%), and Trading Economics' independent CFD series marks $3,336.25 for 10-August (+1.82% on the day, +5.72% on the month, +29.09% year-on-year). BOTH SIT ABOVE THE 13:20 OFFICIAL, which is normal - the official is struck in the second ring while the close and the CFD reflect the full afternoon - and both point the same way: the market kept bidding after the official was set. avg = the JULY-2026 3-month official monthly mean of $3,149.50 computed across the same 23 published July sessions.

kpis.label: Cash-3M spread
kpis.note: THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT NUMBER ON THIS PAGE TODAY. Cash $3,327.50 is ABOVE 3-month $3,320.50, a $7.00 BACKWARDATION, against a $0.50 CONTANGO on 07-August. CONVENTION, STATED EXPLICITLY: cash above 3M is BACKWARDATION and signals prompt tightness; cash below 3M is CONTANGO and signals prompt comfort. THE AUGUST SEQUENCE NOW READS +$48.00, +$34.50, a $0.50 CONTANGO, +$1.00, a $0.50 CONTANGO, and now +$7.00. THIS RESOLVES THE EXACT QUESTION THIS DESK HAD FLAGGED AS THE OPEN TEST FOR FIVE CONSECUTIVE RUNS. Roughly $35/t of front-end structure was written off on 05-August when the Iran-Oman routing announcement was read as the corridor normalising; it then failed to rebuild across four sessions even as flat price made three new highs, and that divergence was the strongest single argument that the rally was positioning rather than physical. IT HAS NOW BEGUN TO REBUILD, AND IT REBUILT ON THE DAY TEHRAN PUBLICLY REPUDIATED THE ASSUMPTION THAT CAUSED IT TO COLLAPSE. PROPORTION MATTERS AND IS NOT BEING OVERSOLD: $7.00 is a THIN backwardation - roughly 0.21% of cash and about a fifth of what was written off on 05-August - it is ONE session old, and single-session structure flips reverse routinely. SPREAD AND FLAT PRICE MOVED IN THE SAME DIRECTION TODAY, which is the confirmation that was absent on 07-August when flat price made a high while the curve slipped into contango. avg = the July-2026 mean cash-3M spread of +$6.48 across the 23 published July sessions, so today's $7.00 is almost exactly the July norm rather than a stress reading - the correct read is REPAIR TO NORMAL, not a squeeze.

lme.commentary: THE RING REOPENED AND DELIVERED THE CONFIRMATION THAT HAD BEEN MISSING. The 10-August official put cash at $3,327.50 (+$48.00, +1.46%) and the 3-month at $3,320.50 (+$40.50, +1.23%) - the largest daily gain of the August sequence, a fourth new cycle high in seven sessions and the highest official cash settlement since 22-June-2026. Across the five August sessions cash has added $131.50 (+4.11%) from the 31-July official. THE STRUCTURE IS THE STORY, NOT THE LEVEL. Cash rose MORE than the 3-month, flipping the curve from a $0.50 CONTANGO on 07-August into a $7.00 BACKWARDATION. Under the convention used throughout this page, cash above 3M is BACKWARDATION and signals prompt tightness. This ends a four-session failure of the front end to rebuild after the 05-August Iran-Oman routing announcement removed roughly $35/t of prompt premium, and it is the first session since 04-August in which spread and flat price moved in the SAME direction. On 07-August the opposite happened - flat price made a seven-week high while the curve slipped into contango - and that divergence was the strongest single argument that the rally was positioning rather than physical. KEEP THE MAGNITUDE HONEST: $7.00 is roughly 0.21% of cash, about a fifth of what was written off on 05-August, one session old, and almost exactly the July average spread of +$6.48. This is a repair to the July norm, not a squeeze, and single-session structure flips reverse routinely. INVENTORY: stock fell 1,500 t to 254,900 t, a 29th consecutive draw and the lowest this century, down 23,375 t (-8.4%) across the 15 sessions charted. But the draw rate is decelerating - 1,500-1,750 t/day over the last five sessions against 2,000-2,400 t/day in late July - and SMM reports China's ingot destocking pace 'narrowing further' at the same time. Two independent inventory systems slowing together is a signal worth holding against the bull case. CROSS-COMPLEX: four of five metals rose on the 3-month official, with copper cash making a fresh 2026 high at $14,290.00 on a further 4,675 t stock draw. Aluminium led a broad advance rather than making a solo high. CHART AXES: the price axis is widened to $3,100-3,400 because cash at $3,327.50 had only $22.50 of headroom under the previous $3,350 ceiling and both the SMM-reported LME close ($3,346.50) and the Trading Economics CFD ($3,336.25) already sit above it. The stock floor is held at 240,000 t, which brackets the series with roughly ten sessions of headroom at the current draw rate.

regional.basis: Q3-2026 SETTLED at $395/t CIF Japan (S&P Global Platts, assessed 06-Jul-2026 off 10 concluded trades totalling a minimum 15,500 mt/month for July-September P1020/P1020A loading; SMM confirmed the same level on 03-Jul) - an 11-year high, prior peak Q3-2014 at $404/t, +11.9-12.9% quarter-on-quarter against Q2's $350-353 range. Offers through those negotiations ranged $440-480/t. PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC, NOT DAILY. A dedicated search this run (11-Aug-2026) returned no new public assessment, settlement or negotiation print for this row. Carrying the last public mark at its stated assessment date is the correct treatment and is not an omission; no figure here has been interpolated, smoothed or re-dated. Q4-2026 talks normally open around late August and conclude late September, so the next hard datapoint for this row is roughly two to three weeks away. THE NEGOTIATING BALANCE SHIFTED TOWARD SELLERS ON 10-AUGUST AND THE MECHANISM IS SPECIFIC. BUYERS' STRONGEST ARGUMENT FOR FIVE SESSIONS WAS THE CURVE, AND IT HAS JUST WEAKENED: the front end had refused to pay for prompt metal since 05-August - two contango prints in five sessions even as flat price made new highs - which is a poor platform from which to argue for a higher regional premium. On 10-August the curve flipped back into a $7.00 BACKWARDATION alongside a $48.00 rise in cash, so the strongest buyer talking point is now one session stale. Buyers retain two real arguments: the yen at roughly 159.1 per dollar raises the local-currency cost of any dollar premium, and the $7.00 backwardation is thin - about 0.21% of cash and roughly a fifth of the $35/t written off on 05-August. SELLERS HOLD THE HARDER PHYSICAL FACTS AND GAINED A DECISIVE ONE ON 10-AUGUST: Iran's Foreign Ministry, via IRNA, stated publicly that the strait will NOT reopen while the US naval posture continues and that Washington 'has no moral or legal standing' to demand a reopening, and separately confirmed that Iran and Oman have STILL not finalised a joint statement on the safe-navigation mechanism. That is the seller of the assumption repudiating it at source: the 05-August routing announcement was priced as the corridor normalising, and the issuing government has now said it is not. The rest of the physical case is unchanged and strong - exchange stock at 254,900 t after a 29th consecutive draw and the lowest this century; Alba's Lines 1, 2 and 3 still under controlled shutdown with Q2 net production down 61% year-on-year; EGA still restoring Al Taweelah cell by cell; commercial transit through the strait at 2 vessels on the last published PortWatch day against a typical 73; war-risk cover for a VLCC at roughly 30 times pre-crisis with six P&I clubs withdrawn; and Brent up 4.19% in 24 hours to $87.85. Underwriters price observed attack frequency and observed transit counts, not communiques, and both moved the sellers' way.

CIF Japan spot reference. PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC, NOT DAILY. A dedicated search this run (11-Aug-2026) returned no new public assessment, settlement or negotiation print for this row. Carrying the last public mark at its stated assessment date is the correct treatment and is not an omission; no figure here has been interpolated, smoothed or re-dated. The carried $370/t spot reference sits $25/t BELOW the settled Q3 quarterly of $395/t. That inversion is informative rather than contradictory: the quarterly was struck on 06-July at the peak of Hormuz supply anxiety, while spot has since traded on thinner, more opportunistic volume. The gap is the clearest single indicator of where the Q4 argument will be fought - buyers will point at spot, sellers at the quarterly and at the physical facts behind it.

A dedicated search this run (11-Aug-2026) returned no new public assessment, settlement or negotiation print for this row. Carrying the last public mark at its stated assessment date is the correct treatment and is not an omission; no figure here has been interpolated, smoothed or re-dated. European premiums remain well supported on the same Gulf-supply logic that drives the Japanese quarterly: Europe is a net importer of primary metal and the Hormuz corridor is the route for a material share of Gulf tonnes. The dated European supply addition to watch is Slovalco - Hydro reached agreement with the Slovak government on 01-July to restart 75,000 t/y, with production expected to start in Q4-2026 - which is the first genuine EU primary capacity return in this cycle.

Carrying the last public mark at its stated assessment date is the correct treatment and is not an omission; no figure here has been interpolated, smoothed or re-dated. Billet upcharges are a separate market from P1020 and move with extrusion order books rather than with ingot tightness. SMM's 11-August briefing notes Chinese aluminium billet processing fees pulled back and billet inventory posted a small build of 4,000 t week-on-week while ingot inventory drew - a divergence that weakens billet's substitution pull on ingot and argues against extrapolating ingot tightness into billet upcharges.

A dedicated search this run (11-Aug-2026) returned no new public assessment, settlement or negotiation print for this row. US premiums are structurally tariff-inflated: the Section 232 leg alone is 0.50 x LME cash = $1,663.75/t at today's settlement, which dwarfs any freight, financing or regional-tightness component. Treat the US rows as a tariff-plus-logistics construct, not as a clean read on physical tightness.

Carrying the last public mark at its stated assessment date is the correct treatment and is not an omission; no figure here has been interpolated, smoothed or re-dated. This is the row the tariff decomposition matches (premium_tariff.us_dp_match). Section 232 rate re-verified this run at 50% on aluminium articles; the April-2026 proclamation applies the tariff to the FULL customs value of covered goods rather than metal content alone, and the June-2026 further adjustment cut the US-content relief threshold from 95% to 85%. At the 10-August cash settlement the tariff leg alone is $1,663.75/t, up $24.00 on the day purely because metal rose.

drivers.text: Tehran repudiated the reopening trade at source on 10-August — Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei stated via IRNA on 10-August that the closure was a response to continued US actions and that Washington 'has no moral or legal standing' to demand a reopening, with reporting the same day that the strait will not reopen while the US naval posture continues. Separately he confirmed Iran and Oman are STILL negotiating the safe-navigation mechanism with NO joint statement finalised. This is the specific assumption that removed roughly $35/t of prompt structure on 05-August being contradicted by the government that made the original announcement. It is the single most important premium input of the last week.
drivers.source: IRNA - US lacks moral or legal standing to demand reopening of Strait (10-Aug-2026)

drivers.text: The curve flipped back into backwardation on the same day - but it is thin — The 10-August official put cash at $3,327.50 against a 3-month of $3,320.50, a $7.00 BACKWARDATION, reversing the $0.50 contango of 07-August and ending a four-session failure of the front end to rebuild. Spread and flat price moved together for the first time in five sessions. Proportion, stated so it is not oversold: $7.00 is about 0.21% of cash, roughly a fifth of what was written off on 05-August, one session old, and almost exactly the July mean of +$6.48 - a repair to normal rather than a squeeze. A premium argument built on one session of structure is fragile.

The physical floor keeps grinding lower but the grind is decelerating — LME stock fell 1,500 t to 254,900 t on 10-August, a 29th consecutive draw and the lowest this century, down 23,375 t (-8.4%) across the 15 sessions on this page. The rate is easing, however: 1,500-1,750 t/day over the last five sessions against 2,000-2,400 t/day in late July. SMM's 11-August briefing reports the same deceleration in China, where ingot social inventory drew 16,000 t week-on-week to 917,000 t with the destocking pace 'narrowing further', while billet inventory built 4,000 t. Tightness is still the direction of travel; the second derivative has turned.

Supply is returning outside China, and that is the structural cap on any Q4 premium — SMM statistics show outside-China aluminium output fell 6.7% year-on-year in July on lower Middle East operating rates, but daily average production ROSE 1.6% month-on-month on resumptions in the Middle East and Iceland plus ramp-ups in Indonesia, Vietnam, India, Brazil, Norway, Spain and Australia. Dated additions include Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026, Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y at New Madrid by year-end, and EGA's cell-by-cell Al Taweelah restart. SMM explicitly notes the renewed Middle East conflict has NOT re-affected smelter production. Premiums priced off a supply shock have to contend with that shock slowly unwinding.
drivers.source: SMM - Some aluminium plants in the Middle East announce production resumptions (31-Jul-2026)

prices.label: Alumina FOB East Australia (SMM reported trade)
prices.note: REFRESHED 11-AUG-2026 AND THERE IS A GENUINELY NEW PUBLIC TRANSACTION THIS RUN. THIS ROW IS HELD AT $356/mt FOB EAST AUSTRALIA (SMM-reported transaction of 30,000 mt for September loading on 05-Aug-2026, published 06-Aug) BECAUSE THE NEW PRINT IS ON A DIFFERENT BASIS AND MUST NOT BE BLENDED INTO IT. THE NEW PRINT: SMM published on 11-August that 30,000 mt of alumina traded at $365/mt CIF MALAYSIA for September shipment, dealt on 07-Aug-2026. CIF MALAYSIA IS A DELIVERED PRICE INCLUDING FREIGHT; FOB EAST AUSTRALIA IS A LOAD-PORT PRICE. The $9/mt gap between them is therefore NOT a $9/mt price rise - on a typical Australia-to-South-East-Asia freight leg the two marks are broadly consistent, and the honest read is that the seaborne market held around the mid-$350s FOB through the first week of August rather than that it rallied. Stating the basis rather than silently splicing the series is the correct treatment. WHAT BOTH MARKS AGREE ON: two independent 30,000 mt seaborne parcels have now printed publicly within three days for September loading, which is the first time this row has had corroboration rather than a single observation. MARGIN CONTEXT: against the 10-August LME 3M official of $3,320.50 the FOB mark sits at about 10.7% of the metal price and the CIF mark at about 11.0%, both comfortably below the decade rule of thumb of roughly 15-17%. On this evidence the alumina leg remains a TAILWIND to smelter economics, not a headwind - and it is the main reason smelter margins are expanding faster than the metal price alone would imply.

prices.label: Alumina API / Platts FOB Australia
prices.note: Platts FOB Australia - NO PUBLIC MARK AT AN AUGUST 2026 DATE. The Platts alumina index and the Fastmarkets MB-ALU-0002 index are subscription products and are not publicly quotable. The last independently verifiable public Platts level is $304/mt on 15-Apr-2026, with Q1-2026 averaging $306.91/mt (-2.82% quarter-on-quarter); the $330/t carried here derives from a 26-Jun reference in S&P Global coverage. The value and date are CARRIED UNCHANGED and are explicitly stale - the two SMM-reported transactions on the row above ($356/mt FOB East Australia dealt 05-Aug, $365/mt CIF Malaysia dealt 07-Aug) are far fresher and should be read as the live market. Both sit well above this carried index level, so the direction of travel since late June has been UP.

prices.label: SMM Alumina Index (China)
prices.note: SMM Alumina Index (China domestic). Carried at its stated date - no fresher public print was returned this run. THE MOST USEFUL NEW CHINESE ALUMINA DATAPOINT THIS RUN IS A COST NUMBER, NOT A PRICE: SMM published on 11-August that China's national weighted-average FULL production cost for alumina was RMB 2,718/mt in July, UP RMB 37/mt month-on-month, with the weighted-average CASH cost at RMB 2,544/mt. SMM guides August full cost to RMB 2,700-2,820/mt and cash cost to RMB 2,530-2,650/mt. The rise is attributed almost entirely to bauxite - higher imported CIF costs on elevated ocean freight plus the Guinea rainy season, and persistently tight domestic ore after mining-accident after-effects slowed restarts - partly offset by a small decline in energy costs. This puts a rising, publicly sourced floor under Chinese alumina and is the mechanism by which bauxite strength transmits into the smelter input basket.

prices.label: Platts FOB Australia (CME futures)
prices.note: CME-listed alumina futures settle against the Platts FOB Australia index. Carried at its stated date; no public settlement series is quotable without a subscription. Directionally the two SMM-reported physical trades this month ($356/mt FOB East Australia, $365/mt CIF Malaysia) and the RMB 37/mt month-on-month rise in Chinese production cost both point the same way - firmer.

prices.label: Bauxite (SMM imported index / Guinea CIF China)
prices.note: Carried at the 06-Aug-2026 SMM Bauxite Weekly Review - no newer weekly review has published at this compile (the cadence is Thursday, so the next print is 13-August). SMM Imported Bauxite Index $71.57/mt, UP $0.70 week-on-week, Guinea CIF $70-74/mt (average +$1 w/w), Guinea FOB $38-42/mt (average +$1 w/w). STRONG NEW CORROBORATION THIS RUN FROM A DIFFERENT SMM PUBLICATION: the 11-August alumina cost review states that imported bauxite prices 'sustained their upward trend in July, serving as the core driver behind the cost surge', citing elevated ocean freight and the Guinea rainy season reducing shipments and lifting arrival costs, plus slow domestic Chinese mine resumption after mining-accident after-effects - to the point that 'some alumina producers have been forced to adjust production schedules'. SMM's forward view: 'no clear timeline has emerged for domestic supply recovery, while imported ore shipments are expected to shrink further amid the rainy season. Bauxite prices are likely to hold high and steady, with import quotes potentially edging slightly higher.' THE NEXT SCHEDULED HARD DATAPOINT REMAINS THE GUINEA AUGUST LONG-TERM CONTRACT, still under negotiation against July's settlement of $70-71.5/mt. DRIVER DOWN, UNCHANGED: Chinese refinery bauxite inventories at roughly 94 days of cover. This is now the best-evidenced upward-trending input on the whole board.

prices.label: Caustic soda (China alumina-plant contract, Shanxi)
prices.note: CNY 2,090/t delivered, 50% ion-membrane liquid on a 100% NaOH basis - the JULY purchase price at Shanxi alumina plants, held flat month-on-month. THE VALUE IS DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED because August contracts have not settled. FRESH FORWARD GUIDANCE THIS RUN AND IT IS WHY THE TREND FLAG MOVES TO UP: SMM's 11-August alumina cost review states that Shanxi caustic soda long-term contract prices are EXPECTED TO RISE BY RMB 50/mt in August, while Guangxi prices are set to DECLINE FURTHER BY RMB 150/mt. That is an explicit regional divergence, not a national move: the north tightens slightly, the south loosens and widens its cost advantage. SMM's assessment of the aggregate effect is that caustic 'had limited impact on alumina production costs' in July and will show 'overall narrow fluctuations' in August. AN EXPECTATION IS NOT A SETTLEMENT: the RMB 50/mt is carried as guidance in this note only and has not been written into the value, which stays at the last settled July figure.

prices.label: Lime / quicklime (China average)
prices.note: China average quicklime for alumina refining, carried at its stated date - no newer public assessment was returned this run and this row has no weekly public series, so gaps stay gaps. Lime is a small share of refinery cash cost and is not a swing factor in the current cost picture; SMM's 11-August cost decomposition attributes July's RMB 37/mt rise to bauxite, with caustic regionally divergent and energy slightly lower, and does not identify lime as a driver.

notes: TWO PUBLIC SEABORNE TRANSACTIONS IN THREE DAYS - THIS ROW FINALLY HAS CORROBORATION. SMM reported 30,000 mt at $356/mt FOB EAST Australia dealt 05-August (published 06-Aug) and, newly published on 11-August, 30,000 mt at $365/mt CIF MALAYSIA dealt 07-August, both for September shipment. Until now the alumina picture rested on a single observation.

THE $9/mt GAP IS A BASIS DIFFERENCE, NOT A PRICE MOVE. CIF Malaysia is delivered and includes freight; FOB East Australia is at the load port. Netted for a typical Australia-to-South-East-Asia freight leg the two are broadly consistent, and the correct conclusion is that the seaborne market HELD around the mid-$350s FOB through the first week of August. Splicing the two into a single series would manufacture a rally that the evidence does not support.

THE COST FLOOR UNDER CHINESE ALUMINA IS RISING AND IT IS NOW PUBLICLY QUANTIFIED. SMM's 11-August cost review puts July's national weighted-average FULL cost at RMB 2,718/mt, up RMB 37/mt month-on-month, and cash cost at RMB 2,544/mt, with August guided to RMB 2,700-2,820 (full) and RMB 2,530-2,650 (cash). The driver is bauxite on both legs - imported CIF costs lifted by ocean freight and the Guinea rainy season, and domestic ore still tight after mining-accident after-effects.

ALUMINA REMAINS A TAILWIND TO SMELTER MARGIN, WHICH IS THE QUIET REASON PRODUCER EARNINGS ARE BEATING SO BROADLY. At $356/mt FOB against the 10-August LME 3M of $3,320.50 the alumina leg is about 10.7% of the metal price, versus a decade rule of thumb of roughly 15-17%. That gap is worth several hundred dollars a tonne of margin across the industry and shows up directly in the peer earnings on this page.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS READ: a third seaborne print materially above $370/mt FOB-equivalent, a Guinea August long-term contract settling well above the July $70-71.5/mt, or Chinese August cost printing at the top of SMM's RMB 2,700-2,820 guide. Any of those would start to compress the margin tailwind. None has printed yet.

logistics.label: Red Sea / Bab al Mandeb corridor
logistics.note: Unchanged in substance and it should not be conflated with Hormuz. Most large container lines moved Asia-Europe services to the Cape of Good Hope as a RED SEA decision, which says nothing about Hormuz transit. Reading the two together overstates the Hormuz effect on containerised trade. Of the nine largest container carriers, 4 advisories describe stopping Hormuz or Gulf service, 3 describe reduced or escorted service still running, and 2 make no claim either way. For aluminium the relevant leg is bulk and breakbulk out of the Gulf, not the container network.

THIS IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT AND IT IS WHY A DIPLOMATIC HEADLINE DOES NOT REOPEN THE CORRIDOR. Underwriters price observed attack frequency and observed transit counts, not communiques. With transits at 2 per day against 73, an oil spill of roughly 390 square kilometres off Oman from a damaged tanker, 14 tankers running AIS-dark in the last 24 hours and Tehran publicly hardening on 10-August, there is nothing in the observable record that would justify an underwriter cutting rates this week. Any premium argument that assumes a rapid normalisation of freight and insurance is arguing against the pricing mechanism itself.

In a closed-corridor regime the commercial risk migrates from price to PERFORMANCE: laytime and demurrage exposure, war-risk clause allocation, and who bears the cost when a vessel cannot obtain cover for a nominated route. With cover at roughly 30 times pre-crisis and six P&I clubs withdrawn, the contractual question of which party carries an uninsurable transit is a live commercial issue across the market, and it is one that a diplomatic communique does not resolve - only a restored insurance market does.

headlines.title: TEHRAN REPUDIATED THE REOPENING TRADE AT SOURCE. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said via state agency IRNA on 10-August that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz was a response to continued US actions and that Washington 'has no moral or legal standing' to demand a reopening; reporting the same day carried the position that the strait will not reopen while the US naval blockade continues. He separately confirmed Iran and Oman are STILL negotiating the safe-navigation mechanism with NO joint statement finalised, and declined to discuss transit fees, saying Iran was 'not discussing such details at this stage'. THIS IS THE DIRECT CONTRADICTION OF THE 05-AUGUST FRAMING that removed roughly $35/t of prompt structure from the aluminium curve. SOURCING CAVEAT STATED PLAINLY: IRNA is Iranian state media and a party to the dispute, so this is a claim rather than independent verification - but the claim itself is the market-relevant fact, because it is the issuing government withdrawing the premise the market had priced.

THE CURVE FLIPPED BACK INTO BACKWARDATION ON THE SAME DAY, ANSWERING THE QUESTION THIS DESK HAD FLAGGED FOR FIVE RUNS. The 10-August official put cash at $3,327.50 against a 3-month of $3,320.50 - a $7.00 BACKWARDATION - reversing the $0.50 CONTANGO of 07-August. Cash rose $48.00 while the 3-month rose $40.50, so the front end outbid the forward curve for the first time since 04-August. Spread and flat price moved in the SAME direction, restoring the confirmation that was absent when flat price made highs into a flattening curve. PROPORTION, SO THIS IS NOT OVERSOLD: $7.00 is about 0.21% of cash, roughly a fifth of what was written off on 05-August, one session old, and almost exactly the July mean of +$6.48. Repair to normal, not a squeeze.

THE COMPLEX CONFIRMED FOUR-TO-ONE, WHICH IS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THIS HIGH AND THE LAST ONE. On the 10-August 3-month official aluminium rose 1.23%, lead 0.63%, copper 0.43% and nickel 0.18%, with only zinc lower at -0.29%. Copper's cash settlement made a FRESH 2026 HIGH at $14,290.00 while its own stock drew a further 4,675 t to 218,300 t, so its price high is corroborated by its physical picture rather than contradicted by it. Contrast 07-August, when aluminium and nickel rose while copper gave back $215.00, zinc fell $72.00 and lead fell $10.50 - a solo aluminium high with no cross-complex support. A rally the whole complex participates in is much harder to dismiss as single-metal positioning.

THE CLEAREST BEARISH INPUT ON THE BOARD IS AT THE LONG END OF THE US CURVE, NOT IN THE PHYSICAL MARKET. SMM's 11-August briefing reports the 30-year US Treasury yield at 5.27%, a 19-YEAR HIGH, with the 10-year at 4.75% and again nearing 5%; Trading Economics marks the 10-year at 4.713% on a separate feed. SMM's own framing of the session is 'liquidity tightening suppresses risk appetite'. Industrial metals are a positioning-sensitive asset class: a 19-year high in long-dated financing costs raises the cost of carrying inventory and of holding commodity length, and is the most plausible mechanism by which this rally stalls without a single physical fact changing. SMM also notes the Fed did not raise in July but retains an overall hawkish stance.

SUPPLY OUTSIDE CHINA IS RETURNING AND THIS IS THE STRUCTURAL CAP ON THE WHOLE TRADE. SMM statistics show outside-China aluminium output fell 6.7% year-on-year in July on lower Middle East operating rates, but DAILY AVERAGE production ROSE 1.6% month-on-month, driven by resumptions in the Middle East and Iceland plus ramp-ups in Indonesia, Vietnam, India, Brazil, Norway, Spain and Australia. SMM states explicitly that the renewed Middle East conflict 'has not affected smelter production again' and expects the month-on-month growth trend to continue in the short term. Dated additions: Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026, Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y at New Madrid by year-end, EGA restoring Al Taweelah cell by cell, Balco ramping in India. COUNTERWEIGHT SMM ITSELF FLAGS: rumours that construction progress on some Middle East and Indonesian projects has fallen short of expectations.

CHINA IS STILL DESTOCKING BUT MORE SLOWLY, AND THE PRICE IS NOW RATIONING DEMAND. SMM's 11-August briefing reports aluminium ingot social inventory down 16,000 t week-on-week to 917,000 t, with the destocking pace 'narrowing further', while BILLET inventory posted a build of 4,000 t. SHFE aluminium closed at 24,190 yuan/mt (+0.64%), a new recent high with a bullish moving-average alignment, and SMM A00 spot at 23,990 yuan/mt (+10). But the demand read is soft: downstream processing is in its traditional consumption off-season with total operating rates under pressure, prices above 24,000 yuan/mt are 'somewhat suppressing downstream procurement', purchase willingness is 'subdued' and billet processing fees pulled back, weakening substitution demand for ingot. Central China transactions cleared at a 120-140 yuan/mt DISCOUNT to the August contract. The bid is coming from traders and arbitrage rather than from consumers - a real distinction and a genuine caution on the rally's quality.

TWO PUBLIC SEABORNE ALUMINA TRADES IN THREE DAYS, AND THE COST FLOOR UNDER CHINESE ALUMINA IS NOW QUANTIFIED. SMM published on 11-August that 30,000 mt traded at $365/mt CIF MALAYSIA for September shipment, dealt 07-August - corroborating the 30,000 mt at $356/mt FOB EAST AUSTRALIA dealt 05-August. THE $9/mt GAP IS A BASIS DIFFERENCE, NOT A RALLY: CIF is delivered and includes freight, FOB is at the load port, and netted for freight the two are broadly consistent. SEPARATELY SMM PUT NUMBERS ON THE COST SIDE: China's national weighted-average FULL alumina production cost was RMB 2,718/mt in July, up RMB 37/mt month-on-month, cash cost RMB 2,544/mt, with August guided to RMB 2,700-2,820/mt full. The driver is bauxite - higher imported CIF on elevated ocean freight and the Guinea rainy season, plus tight domestic ore after mining-accident after-effects, 'forcing some alumina producers to adjust production schedules'. MIXED because a rising alumina cost floor is bullish for the alumina price but a headwind to smelter margin - though at roughly 10.7% of the metal price, alumina is still a long way below its 15-17% decade norm and remains a net margin tailwind.

BRENT JUMPED 4.19% IN 24 HOURS TO $87.85 ON THE SAME HORMUZ HARDENING, roughly 22% above the pre-crisis reference of about $72, with Trading Economics marking $87.83 on an independent feed and European TTF gas at EUR 61.53/MWh (+1.21%). THIS IS NOT MERELY A SENTIMENT READ - IT IS A COST INPUT. Energy is 30-40% of smelter cash cost, more than every other input on this board combined, so a sustained crude move lifts the global cost floor, feeds calcined petroleum coke and coal tar pitch into the 17th-18th monthly settlement window, and feeds bauxite ocean freight immediately. SMM's 11-August cost review names elevated freight as a core driver of the RMB 37/mt rise in Chinese alumina production cost. A rising cost floor beneath a supply-constrained metal is a durable support, not a transient one.

THE PHYSICAL CORRIDOR IS NO CLOSER TO REOPENING AND THE INSURANCE MARKET IS THE REASON. IMF PortWatch recorded 2 commercial transits on 02-August, its most recent published day, against a pre-crisis norm of about 73 per day - roughly 3% of normal. War-risk cover for a VLCC is estimated at roughly 30 times pre-crisis with a per-voyage premium of the order of $10m, and six P&I clubs have withdrawn cover entirely. 14 tankers ran AIS-dark in the last 24 hours. On 10-August Oman reported an oil slick of roughly 390 square kilometres from a damaged sanctioned tanker - on the exact southern corridor the Iran-Oman talks propose for outbound traffic. UNDERWRITERS PRICE OBSERVED ATTACK FREQUENCY AND OBSERVED TRANSIT COUNTS, NOT COMMUNIQUES, so any view that assumes rapid normalisation of Gulf freight is arguing against the pricing mechanism itself. Prediction markets concur: Polymarket prices normal traffic by 31-August at 3%, by 31-December at 47%; Kalshi prices a 7-day transit average above 60 before 01-October at 12%.

A 29TH CONSECUTIVE LME DRAW TO 254,900 t, THE LOWEST THIS CENTURY - BUT THE RATE IS DECELERATING AND THAT DESERVES EQUAL BILLING. Stock fell 1,500 t on 10-August and is down 23,375 t (-8.4%) across the 15 sessions on this page, from 278,275 t on 21-July, and roughly a third since January. THE SECOND DERIVATIVE HAS TURNED: the last five sessions have drawn 1,500-1,750 t per day against 2,000-2,400 t per day in late July, and SMM reports the same deceleration in China where the ingot destocking pace is 'narrowing further'. Two independent inventory systems slowing at the same time is a signal, not noise. The direction of travel is still tightening; the intensity is fading. That is exactly the configuration in which a backwardation appears and then struggles to widen.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. earnings.readthrough: THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. This map is reviewed monthly or on material change and is deliberately not churned daily. An oil slick of roughly 390 square kilometres off Oman from a damaged sanctioned tanker adds a navigational complication on the exact southern corridor the talks propose for outbound traffic. THE GENERIC COMMERCIAL POINT: the binding constraint on these lanes is the insurance market, not the diplomatic channel. Underwriters reprice on observed attack frequency and observed transit counts, which is why the 05-August announcement moved the aluminium curve by roughly $35/t while the physical corridor did not follow. This is the single highest-information event on the calendar because it tests the one thing that changed yesterday. Three reads in order of value: (1) does the cash-3M spread HOLD or widen beyond $7.00, confirming that prompt demand rather than a headline drove Monday's flip - or does it collapse back into contango as it did on 05 and 07 August; (2) does the stock draw continue and at what rate, given the last five sessions have decelerated to 1,500-1,750 t/day; (3) does the complex stay together, or does aluminium go back to making solo highs while copper and zinc fade. A second consecutive backwardation with a continued draw would materially strengthen the physical case. A return to contango would place the whole 10-August move back in the positioning column.

SMM BAUXITE WEEKLY REVIEW. The cadence is Thursday and the last print was 06-August at an SMM Imported Bauxite Index of $71.57/mt (+$0.70 w/w), Guinea CIF $70-74/mt. SMM's forward view is that 'imported ore shipments are expected to shrink further amid the rainy season' and that 'import quotes potentially edging slightly higher'. MONTHLY CARBON SETTLEMENT WINDOW - PREBAKED ANODES, CALCINED PETROLEUM COKE AND COAL TAR PITCH. Prebaked anodes are the largest non-energy line in the smelter input basket and the July mark of RMB 5,683/t stands until this settles. risks.text: THE BACKWARDATION IS ONE SESSION OLD AND THIN, AND A SECOND CONTANGO PRINT WOULD RESET THE WHOLE BULL ARGUMENT. The $7.00 prompt premium restored on 10-August is roughly 0.21% of cash and about a fifth of the ~$35/t removed on 05-August. The August sequence has already produced two contango prints in six sessions, so a single-session flip has demonstrably reversed before. The specific risk is that 10-August was a one-day response to a headline rather than a change in physical demand for prompt metal: the underlying draw rate is decelerating (1,500-1,750 t/day against 2,000-2,400 t/day in late July), China's destocking pace is 'narrowing further' per SMM, and Chinese cargo is clearing at a 120-140 yuan/mt DISCOUNT to futures. TODAY'S 13:20 RING IS THE CLEAN TEST. WHY THE TREND IS 'DOWN': the risk this desk carried for five runs - that the front end would not rebuild at all - has been partially resolved in the bullish direction, so the risk is materially reduced from yesterday. It is reduced, not eliminated.

SUPPLY OUTSIDE CHINA IS RETURNING FASTER THAN THE PRICE NARRATIVE ADMITS, AND THIS IS THE MOST UNDER-PRICED BEARISH FACT ON THE PAGE. SMM statistics show outside-China DAILY AVERAGE aluminium production ROSE 1.6% month-on-month in July, even though the year-on-year total fell 6.7%, driven by resumptions in the Middle East and Iceland and ramp-ups in Indonesia, Vietnam, India, Brazil, Norway, Spain and Australia. SMM states explicitly that the renewed Middle East conflict 'has not affected smelter production again' and expects the month-on-month growth trend to continue. Dated additions: Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026, Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y at New Madrid by year-end, EGA restoring Al Taweelah cell by cell, Balco expanding in India. A market priced on a supply shock is exposed to that shock unwinding on a published schedule. TREND UP: another month of month-on-month growth was confirmed this cycle.

THE 30-YEAR US TREASURY YIELD AT A 19-YEAR HIGH IS THE CLEANEST MECHANISM BY WHICH THIS RALLY STALLS WITHOUT A SINGLE PHYSICAL FACT CHANGING. SMM's 11-August briefing puts the 30-year at 5.27% and the 10-year at 4.75%, framing the session as 'liquidity tightening suppresses risk appetite'; Trading Economics marks the 10-year at 4.713% on an independent feed. The Fed held in July but SMM characterises the stance as hawkish overall. Industrial metals are positioning-sensitive: long-dated financing costs at generational highs raise the cost of carrying inventory and of holding commodity length, and hit hardest exactly when a rally is being carried by financial rather than consumer demand - which is the case here. TREND UP: yields rose into a fresh 19-year high this session.

END DEMAND IS THE WEAKEST LINK AND THE PRICE IS NOW VISIBLY RATIONING IT. SMM reports Chinese downstream processing in its traditional consumption off-season with total operating rates under pressure, prices above 24,000 yuan/mt 'somewhat suppressing downstream procurement', purchase willingness 'subdued', billet processing fees pulling back and billet inventory BUILDING 4,000 t week-on-week while ingot drew. Central China cargo cleared at a 120-140 yuan/mt DISCOUNT to the August contract, and SMM attributes the bid to traders and spot-futures arbitrage rather than to consumers. A rally whose marginal buyer is an arbitrageur is structurally more fragile than one whose marginal buyer is a fabricator. TREND UP: the billet build and the widening scrap-to-primary spread both worsened this week.

A CREDIBLE HORMUZ REOPENING REMAINS THE LARGEST SINGLE DOWNSIDE PRICE RISK, BUT IT MOVED FURTHER AWAY ON 10-AUGUST. The 05-August routing announcement alone removed roughly $35/t of prompt structure within a session, which is a live demonstration of how much of this price is geopolitical premium. On 10-August Iran's Foreign Ministry stated the strait will not reopen while the US naval posture continues, said Washington has no standing to demand it, confirmed no joint statement with Oman has been finalised, and declined to discuss transit fees; President Trump separately described reciprocal compensation demands now written into all future negotiations. Prediction markets moved with it: Polymarket prices normal traffic by 31-August at 3% and by 31-December at 47%; Kalshi prices a 7-day transit average above 60 before 01-October at 12%. TREND DOWN: the near-term probability of the bearish trigger fell this session. It has NOT gone away - the 47% December contract says the market still expects resolution within the year.

THE PHYSICAL TIGHTENING IS DECELERATING ON BOTH SIDES OF THE WORLD SIMULTANEOUSLY, WHICH IS EASY TO MISS BEHIND A HEADLINE 29TH CONSECUTIVE DRAW. LME stock fell 1,500 t to 254,900 t, but the last five sessions have averaged 1,500-1,750 t/day against 2,000-2,400 t/day in late July. In China, SMM reports ingot social inventory down 16,000 t week-on-week to 917,000 t with the destocking pace 'narrowing further', and down 41,000 t from the prior Monday - i.e. the weekly rate roughly halved. Two independent inventory systems slowing at the same time is a signal rather than noise. The direction of travel is still tightening; the intensity is fading, and that is precisely the configuration in which a backwardation appears and then fails to widen. TREND UP: the deceleration became clearer on both series this week.

THE AUGUST CARBON SETTLEMENT AROUND THE 17TH-18TH IS THE NEXT SCHEDULED MARGIN EVENT AND BOTH FEEDSTOCK LEGS POINT UP. Prebaked anodes are the largest non-energy line in the smelter input basket and settle monthly with calcined petroleum coke and coal tar pitch. Brent at $87.85 after a 4.19% daily gain feeds green coke through refinery economics, and coal at $129.00 is up 14.92% year-on-year, feeding coal tar pitch. A high August anode settlement landing while metal stalls would compress the margin expansion that is currently driving the peer earnings on this page. TREND UP: both feedstock proxies rose into the settlement window.

ALUMINA'S COST FLOOR IS RISING AND BAUXITE IS THE DRIVER, WHICH THREATENS THE QUIETEST SUPPORT UNDER PRODUCER MARGINS. SMM's 11-August review puts China's July weighted-average FULL alumina production cost at RMB 2,718/mt, up RMB 37/mt month-on-month, with August guided to RMB 2,700-2,820/mt, attributing the rise almost entirely to bauxite: higher imported CIF on elevated ocean freight, the Guinea rainy season reducing shipments, and domestic Chinese ore still tight after mining-accident after-effects to the point that 'some alumina producers have been forced to adjust production schedules'. SMM expects import quotes to edge higher. Alumina is still only about 10.7% of the metal price against a 15-17% decade norm, so this is a compression risk rather than a margin threat today. TREND UP: the cost rise was quantified and the forward guide is higher.

DATA-INTEGRITY RISK IS ACTIVE, NOT THEORETICAL, AND IT MATERIALISED AGAIN THIS RUN. On first fetch the Westmetall per-metal ALUMINIUM and NICKEL tables served a stale 07-August snapshot while both language overviews already carried 10-August; cache-busted re-fetches returned the correct 10-August rows, which then matched the overviews exactly. That is the third distinct cache incident logged (31-Jul per-metal tables, 04-Aug English overview, 11-Aug per-metal tables). A single-source compile on this board would have published a stale session and reported a flat day when the market moved $48.00. The mitigation - fetching English overview, German overview and cache-busted per-metal tables and requiring exact agreement - caught it for the third time. TREND FLAT: recurring at a steady rate, and the control is working.
